topPRs.title: docs: regenerate op-reth CLI reference at v2.4.1 via new gen-op-reth-cli pipeline (IA slice 9)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

IA-modernization slice 9 (final slice of the lane) per [`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/solutions/blob/main/projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md): the op-reth CLI regeneration pipeline, plus its first regeneration at `op-reth/v2.4.1`.

## Before / After

**Before:** the 59-page op-reth CLI reference was a one-time snapshot of the retired Vocs site with no regeneration pipeline. It silently drifted from every op-reth release — missing whole command families (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`), documenting seven `db settings set` subcommands the binary no longer has, and carrying stale flags and help text on 51 pages.

**After:** the reference is regenerated from the current finalized release (`op-reth/v2.4.1`) and gains a documented, review-gated regeneration pipeline for future releases. Readers get 21 new command pages (including the whole `proofs` family), 51 corrected pages, and the 7 retired pages redirect to the surviving `db settings set` page that documents the replacement `v2` flow. The hand-written CLI overview gains one table row (`proofs`).

## How

- **Pipeline** — new `docs/public-docs/scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/` (`main.mjs` + `README.md` + `manifest.json`): a zero-dependency Node port of upstream reth's `docs/cli/update.sh` + `docs/cli/help.rs` (the exact tooling whose output format the original snapshot matches). It walks a pinned release binary's `--help` tree and emits the MDX pages (`diataxis: reference` frontmatter), the docs.json nav fragment for the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group (hand-written `cli/overview` guarded as the group's first entry, never touched), and provenance in `manifest.json`. Environment-dependent help output (home paths, version/target triples, CPU-count defaults) is scrubbed with upstream's replacement set.
- **Provenance chain** — binary built from source at tag `op-reth/v2.4.1` (tag commit `a9a8dad3f15`, the latest finalized non-rc release), which pins upstream reth at rev `f2eecc65482a`. `manifest.json` records `{tag, binaryVersion, sha256-over-generated-tree}`.
- **Idempotency** — running the generator twice against the same binary is a byte-for-byte no-op (verified live: second run reports `0 new, 0 changed, removed 0`, `git status` clean). `--check` mode recomputes the whole tree in memory and fails on any divergence, so hand edits to generated pages cannot survive review.

## No CI wiring (per Matthew's ruling)

Nothing in this diff touches `.circleci/`, `.github/`, or any package script; nothing runs unattended. Regeneration is registered as a **review-gated Mintlify docs automation** (see the README's "Automation registration" section, mirroring the gen-flags precedent in `DOCS_CONTRIBUTING.md`): when a newer finalized `op-reth/v*` tag exists than the manifest's, a regeneration is *proposed for human review* — never merged by CI. All 79 changed files live under `docs/public-docs/`.

## Regeneration drift (first run at v2.4.1)

| Kind | Count | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New pages | 21 | `proofs` family (7 pages), `db copy`, `db migrate-v2`, `db state`, `db prune-checkpoints` (3), `db stage-checkpoints` (3), `db checksum rocksdb`, `db get rocksdb`, `db settings set v2`, `p2p enode` |
| Updated pages | 51 | Genuine drift: new flags (e.g. `--tx-channel-memory-limit`, `--rpc.disable-metrics`, `--rpc-cache.max-bals`), renames (`--enable-discv5-discovery` → `--disable-discv5-discovery`), help-text and `--chain` list changes |
| Deleted pages | 7 | The per-table `db settings set <table>` leaves, superseded upstream by `db settings set v2` |
| Nav entries | 409 → 423 | +21 / −7; all other tabs and groups byte-identical, tab count 8 → 8 |

## Redirects (645 → 652)

| Change | Count | Detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| New (R5, one per deleted page) | 7 | `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/db/settings/set/<table>` → `.../db/settings/set` (the surviving parent documenting the `v2` flow) |
| Retargeted in place | 9 | The legacy `/rust/op-reth/cli/.../db/settings/set/<table>` entries (7 + 2 `*_in_static_files`) each pointed at a now-deleted URL; retargeted to `.../db/settings/set` so no chains or stale destinations exist |

Full 652-entry trace: 0 duplicate sources, 0 chains, 0 sources shadowing live pages, 0 destinations pointing at deleted URLs; no prose page links to any deleted URL.

## Deviations from the plan (stated plainly)

1. **7 redirects vs the plan's ~0–5 budget** — the estimate predates further months of upstream drift; every removal is the single superseded `db settings set` per-table family, all covered same-PR per R5 (plus the 9 in-place retargets the no-chain rule requires).
2. **Binary built from source (dev profile) instead of the release Docker image** — the release ships no binary assets and the image registry is egress-blocked in the build environment. Feature set matches the official image build (default features = DockerfileOp set); clap `--help` output is feature-dependent, not profile-dependent. Release metadata was injected exactly as the official image build does.
3. **One fork-specific scrub beyond upstream `help.rs`** — `default: op-reth/<VERSION>-<SHA>/<ARCH>`: the fork identifies as `op-reth/...` where upstream's scrub patterns only cover the `reth/...` spelling; without it the build-host arch would leak into a page. Recorded in `main.mjs` comments and the README.
4. **`manifest.json` carries `binaryVersion`** in addition to the gen-flags-precedent `{tag, sha256}` — extra provenance for a binary-derived generator.

## Verification (re-derived independently by the verifier)

- `--check` against the tag binary: exit 0 — 72 pages, nav fragment, and manifest all match the `--help` tree; manifest sha256 `e979848d9b4a…9017f6ad` re-derived independently and matches.
- `op-reth/v2.4.1` confirmed as the latest finalized (non-rc, non-draft) op-reth release via the GitHub API; `rust/Cargo.toml` at the tag pins reth rev `f2eecc65482a`.
- Sample pages (`proofs`, `db migrate-v2`, `p2p enode`, `node`, `db list`, `config`): flag sets match the binary's `--help` exactly; the 7 deleted commands are absent from the binary (`db settings set` now has only `v2`).
- Leakage sweep over all 72 pages: zero hits for the version string, commit SHAs, build timestamps, target triples, or build-host paths.
- Lints: `validate-nav.ts` OK (424 pages on disk / 423 nav entries / 1 allowlisted orphan — counts reconcile exactly), `validate-redirects.ts` OK (652 redirects, 11 grandfathered — baseline byte-identical to how IA-8 left it), `lint-link-policy.mjs` 0 findings. All 73 touched MDX files compile clean under @mdx-js/mdx.

## Wiz SAST findings (8 LOW) — addressed

Wiz flagged 8 LOW SAST findings on the PR head. The only SAST-scannable code in this diff is `scripts/gen-op-reth-cli/main.mjs` (everything else is MDX/JSON/Markdown), and its sinks account for exactly the two pattern classes Wiz LOW-flags in JavaScript: two `child_process` executions (`execFileSync` for `--help`/`--version`) and six dynamic-path `fs` operations (page write/mkdir/delete, docs.json write, manifest read/write, existing-page reads).

Context: this is a repo-local, review-gated generator that only shells out to a binary the operator explicitly passes via `--bin` (built locally from a release tag); it already used `execFileSync` with argument arrays (no shell), and every dynamic path is rooted at script-relative constants. The one genuine untrusted-input flow — subcommand names parsed from the binary's `--help` output feed both process arguments and file paths — is now hardened in `06bcbc29c9`: names are validated against the shape clap actually produces (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$/`, run aborts on anything else), and every page write/delete asserts containment inside the generated tree. No behavior change: `--check` still passes byte-identically at v2.4.1. The remaining dynamic-path reads/writes against script-relative constants (docs.json, manifest.json) are inherent to any generator and not reachable from untrusted input.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Preview: the collapsed "op-reth CLI reference" group under Node Operators → Reference renders with `overview` first and nested subgroups in `--help` order (eyeball `db settings set` → `set`, `v2`)
- [ ] Spot-check a new page (e.g. `/node-operators/op-reth/cli/op-reth/proofs`) against `op-reth proofs --help` at v2.4.1
- [ ] Hit a deleted URL (e.g. `.../db/settings/set/receipts`) and confirm the redirect lands on `.../db/settings/set`
- [ ] Confirm the README's automation-registration section matches the intended Mintlify registry entry (review-gated, never CI)
- [ ] Agree the 4 deviations above are acceptable

## Program status

This closes the IA-modernization lane: slices 1–9 have all shipped. D12 is the program's last remaining content slice.

topPRs.title: op-reth: recover proof history gaps on startup
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Closes #22089.

## Summary

- seed the historical-proofs engine's catch-up target from the durable execution head on every startup
- recover proof blocks lost from the in-memory, below-threshold tail without waiting for another canonical-chain notification
- add a black-box restart test that starts with execution durably at block 3 and proofs at genesis, then verifies `debug_proofsSyncStatus` catches up without producing a new block

The collector previously started with `sync_target = 0`. If shutdown lost blocks that had been acknowledged via `FinishedHeight` but not persisted, restart had no event that could raise the target: the blocks were already canonical and produced no new ExEx notification. Seeding the existing catch-up path from `best_block_number()` makes the persisted proof tip the effective recovery checkpoint and works after unclean shutdown as well as clean-shutdown tail loss.

This complements #22090's clean-shutdown flush with startup recovery for crashes and other durable execution/proofs divergence.

## Tests

- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-node`
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo nextest run -p reth-optimism-exex`
- `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo clippy -p reth-optimism-exex -p reth-optimism-node --tests --all-features -- -D warnings`

topPRs.title: docs: merge the standard-bridge token tutorials into "Create an L2 token for the Standard Bridge" (dedup D7: T17)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

## Before / After

Before: the docs had two near-duplicate "bridge a token" tutorials, one for standard tokens and one for custom tokens, that were 51% the same page (duplication census cluster T17). Readers had to pick between two siblings that shared the same setup, the same test token, the same bridging pointer, and the same Superchain Token List section, and each page told them to go read the other one if they picked wrong.

After: one tutorial, "Create an L2 token for the Standard Bridge", at the existing `standard-bridge-standard-token` URL, sitting first in the Bridging tutorials group. The intro explains the standard-vs-custom choice up front, all shared sections exist once, and the two deployment flows live side by side as tabs ("Standard token" via `cast` and the factory, "Custom token" via Remix) in the "Create an L2 ERC-20 token" section. The old `standard-bridge-custom-token` URL redirects to the merged page.

## How

* `standard-bridge-standard-token.mdx` rewritten as the merged tutorial; both old Steps flows carried into their tabs (contract code, deploy parameters, and cast commands byte-identical to the source pages); the custom page's withdrawal caveat kept, now explicitly scoped to the custom example token.
* `standard-bridge-custom-token.mdx` deleted; 1 redirect appended to `docs.json` and 1 nav entry removed (632 to 633 redirects, no duplicate sources, no chains, no stale destinations).
* The standard tab's private-key step now renders the shared `TutorialSetupWalletAndFunds` snippet (D2) instead of a hand-written copy of the same text; the fee-on-transfer warning arrives once via the D10 snippet.
* Six inbound references repointed (`implement-a-custom-deposit-flow` twice, `cross-dom-bridge-erc20`, `standard-bridge`, `basics`, `custom-bridge`); the two-link tutorial lists collapse to one "standard or custom" link. Two snippet consumer-list comments updated. A repo-wide grep for the old path now matches only the redirect source.

## Fact corrections folded in

* The old custom page linked the text `IOptimismMintableERC20` to `OptimismMintableERC20Factory.sol`, which does not define that interface. The merged page links `packages/contracts-bedrock/interfaces/universal/IOptimismMintableERC20.sol`, the file that defines it (verified on develop at the base commit).
* The old custom page listed `node` and `pnpm` as dependencies, but its flow is Remix-only in the browser and contains no terminal commands at all. The merged Dependencies section lists `cast` for the standard path and a browser wallet for the custom path.

One pre-existing inconsistency was deliberately NOT fixed here (carried verbatim, out of merge scope): the custom example contract pins `pragma solidity 0.8.20` while the compile step says to use compiler 0.8.15. Queued to the accuracy lane on ethereum-optimism/solutions#1172 (Finding-ID `8550c94e1d195542`).

## Review feedback addressed (sbvegan)

The first cut of this PR titled the merged page "Bridge tokens with the Standard Bridge", which was misleading: the page teaches how to create an L2 representation of an L1 token that works with the Standard Bridge, then hands off to the viem tutorial for the actual bridging. Follow-up commit:

* Retitled the page to "Create an L2 token for the Standard Bridge" and rewrote the description to match (same URL, no new redirects).
* Reframed the intro to state plainly what the reader builds (an L2 token contract on OP Sepolia that the Standard Bridge can mint and burn) and that bridging itself lives in [Bridging ERC-20 tokens with viem](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/public-docs/app-developers/tutorials/bridging/cross-dom-bridge-erc20.mdx).
* Moved the page to the FIRST position in the Bridging tutorials nav group.
* Updated the two inbound links that reused the old title (`implement-a-custom-deposit-flow`, `cross-dom-bridge-erc20`); the other four repointed references already said "create a bridged token".

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] **A human walkthrough of both tabs on the Mintlify preview is required before merge.** The end-to-end tutorial was NOT executable from this environment (no funded Sepolia / OP Sepolia wallet), so the plan's "executed end-to-end with a run log" acceptance criterion is open. All commands and contract addresses are byte-identical to the two source pages, but nobody has re-run them for this PR.
- [ ] Both tabs render correctly (Tabs / Steps nesting) and the intro's `#create-an-l2-erc-20-token` anchor resolves on the rendered page.
- [ ] Old URL `/app-developers/tutorials/bridging/standard-bridge-custom-token` redirects to the merged page on the preview.
- [ ] No unique content lost: verifier diffed the merged page against both source pages section by section (all code blocks byte-identical; every prose instruction carried or covered).
- [ ] Lints: nav validator OK (409 pages / 408 nav entries), redirect lint OK (633 redirects, zero new findings), link-policy lint zero findings.

## Sequencing

This PR holds the serialized `docs.json` slot for the docs-improver program: IA-4 (App Developers skeleton re-parent) queues behind it and should not start its `docs.json` edit until this merges.

Tracking: ethereum-optimism/solutions (docs-improver iteration-2 dedup D7).

topPRs.title: docs: App Developers + Chain Operators tab skeletons and index pages (IA slice 4)
topPRs.author: claude
topPRs.body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
_Requested by **Matthew Cruz** · [Slack thread](https://oplabs-pbc.slack.com/archives/C0BHEH8TG91/p1784834359611159?thread_ts=1784834359.611159&cid=C0BHEH8TG91)_

Slice 4 of the iteration-2 IA modernization plan (`projects/docs-improver/plans/iteration-2/ia-modernization.md` in ethereum-optimism/solutions): the last two audience tabs get the same Diátaxis skeleton as the rest of the site, plus proper landing pages.

## Before / After (what a reader sees)

**Before:**
- The App Developers sidebar had 8 top-level groups, with Bridging, Interoperability, and Transactions each appearing twice at different nesting levels (as a top-level guide group and again as a Tutorials subgroup, meaning different things each time).
- Neither App Developers nor Chain Operators had a tab landing page: clicking the tab dumped visitors straight into the first article.

**After:**
- App Developers has the same 5-group skeleton as the other tabs (Get started / Guides / Tutorials / Tools & SDKs / Reference), with Bridging, Interoperability, and Transactions now subgroups under Guides. No label appears at two different nesting levels anymore.
- Both tabs open on a short Overview landing page (`/app-developers`, `/chain-operators`) that routes readers by what they came to do: quickstart, guides, tutorials, tools, reference, plus a catch-all back to the site root.
- Zero URL changes, so zero redirects. Every existing page keeps its address and stays in the nav.

## How

- `docs.json`: nav-only re-parenting inside the App Developers tab (3 guide groups moved intact under Guides, page order preserved; Tutorials subgroups reordered to Bridging / Interoperability / Supersim / Transactions; the 2 Quickstarts pages regrouped under the new Get started group behind the index). Chain Operators only gains a Get started group holding its new index page.
- 2 new pages, both following the published router/landing contract (`op-stack/contribute/router-landing.mdx`): `content-type: router-landing`, `last-reviewed`, one orienting paragraph, cards with resolving hrefs, catch-all route.
- Nav entry count 408 → 410 (+2, exactly the two index pages). Redirects array untouched (633 entries, byte-identical to develop).

## Deviations from the plan (stated plainly)

1. **Quickstarts folded into Get started.** The 2-page Quickstarts group postdates the plan; leaving it would put two synonym get-started groups back to back. Its pages keep their URLs and now sit under Get started after the index page. Reversible with a 3-line nav edit if reviewers prefer it separate.
2. **`content-type: router-landing` instead of the plan's literal `diataxis:` frontmatter.** The plan delegates authoring to the published content-type contracts, and the (post-plan) router/landing contract states a pure router carries no `diataxis:` key. Every existing router in the tree follows that contract; these two do the same.
3. **The App Developers Reference card routes to `reference/rpc-providers`, not the group's first page `reference/networks`.** `networks.mdx` is 193 bytes and one of the plan's named fill-or-delist candidates for slice 8; pointing a brand-new curated router at it would manufacture a future broken or redirected link.

## Reviewer checklist

- [ ] Mintlify preview: App Developers tab opens on the new Overview page (not verifiable from the authoring environment; both index pages are the first nav entry of their tab's first group, which is the convention the live Node Operators tab relies on)
- [ ] Mintlify preview: Chain Operators tab opens on the new Overview page (same caveat)
- [ ] Mintlify preview: both landing pages render the 6-card grid and all card links resolve
- [ ] Sidebar group order: App Developers = Get started / Guides / Tutorials / Tools & SDKs / Reference; Chain Operators = Get started / Guides / Tutorials / Tools / Reference / Archive
- [ ] No label appears at two nesting levels of the App Developers sidebar
- [ ] Lints: `validate-nav.ts` (410 nav entries, 1 allowlisted orphan), `validate-redirects.ts` (633, unchanged), link-policy lint (0 findings), both new pages MDX-compile

## Sequencing

This PR holds the serialized `docs.json` queue slot (queue 9 in the merged program order); IA slice 5 (OP Mainnet) queues behind it.

topPRs.title: op-conductor: route raft logs through application logger
topPRs.author: Kemperino
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- route HashiCorp Raft logs through op-conductor's configured application logger
- apply the existing log level and formatting to Raft core, snapshot, and network logs
- preserve Raft subsystem names and severity when forwarding records

## Root cause

`raft.DefaultConfig` defaults to debug logging and creates an independent logger on stderr when no logger is provided. Op-conductor left that logger unset, so Raft logs bypassed `--log.level` and could be classified as errors by log collectors based on their stderr stream.

## Impact

Raft logs now respect op-conductor's configured log level and use the same structured output path as the rest of the service. With the default info level, Raft debug logs are suppressed instead of being emitted independently to stderr.

## Validation

- `just lint-go` (`0 issues`)
- `go test ./op-conductor/...`
- `go vet ./op-conductor/...`
- `go mod tidy -diff`
